Scholarly Name Reference

भैषज्यगुरु Bhaiṣajyaguru

also written Bhaisajyaguru

'Medicine master' (bhaiṣajya 'healing, remedy' + guru 'teacher'), the Medicine Buddha of lapis-lazuli radiance who vows to cure the sick.

The Authentic Name of Bhaiṣajyaguru

Scholarly reference for Bhaiṣajyaguru

Devanagari

भैषज्यगुरु

The name in its original Devanagari form. भैषज्यगुरु → Bhaiṣajyaguru. Sanskrit Bhaiṣajyaguru is written in Devanagari as भैषज्यगुरु · IAST transliteration maps each Devanagari vowel and consonant to a Latin equivalent · Macrons mark long vowels (ā, ī, ū); dots beneath consonants mark retroflex articulation (ṭ, ḍ, ṇ, ṣ)

ASCII Constraint

BHAISAJYAGURU

Stripped of its identity, the name was reduced to plain Latin letters. The original orthography — stress, length, breathing — was erased by systems that only understand A-Z.

Unicode Restoration

Bhaiṣajyaguru

The Unicode restoration recovers what ASCII destroyed. This is philological accuracy — not decoration. The domain encodes to Punycode, but the browser displays the truth.

Punycode Encoding
bhaiṣajyaguru.com → xn--bhaiajyaguru-6g5f.com

The non-ASCII characters in Bhaiṣajyaguru are encoded while the ASCII remains visible. To the DNS, it is Punycode. To humanity, it is Bhaiṣajyaguru. PUNICODEX does not claim this domain is available; always verify status with a registrar.

Tier Classification

The Buddhist restoration भैषज्यगुरु preserves at least one distinctive feature its ASCII form loses — a diacritic or a distinctive letter that marks the original phonology. This makes it a single-tier Tier-1 name.
